data.narrative:
Inversion Space is a Series A-stage housing and construction company founded by Justin Fiaschetti and Austin Briggs. The company has raised $44M to date. The applicable comp universe is limited to two private peers—Cobod and Material Evolution—with no public comps available in this subsector, reflecting the early-stage and fragmented nature of frontier construction technology.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $44M total raised proxy, reflecting typical step-up economics from Series A to the next funding round. This method yields an implied valuation of $88M. The 2.0x multiplier captures expected value creation between rounds but remains conservative given execution risk at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $75M (low) to $101M (high), with a median of $88M. The narrow methodology applied—one primary method—reflects data constraints; the absence of public comps and the small peer set limit triangulation depth. Key uncertainties include unit economics in the target market segment, competitive positioning relative to Cobod and Material Evolution, and path to cash flow sustainability. Investors should weight execution risk heavily given the stage and the limited comparable transaction history in this subsector.
